answer.policy_title: Spinal Fusion and Decompression (for Idaho Only) [UHC Community Plan] / Cervical Fusion Prior Authorization Requirements Checklist [Blue Cross of Idaho]
criteria_quotes: If conservative treatment was completed, please provide documentation of 6 weeks of Conservative Therapy which should include the following:
The use of prescription oral analgesic medications, preferably anti-inflammatories.
Documented participation in a formal, active physical therapy program with notes from a licensed physical therapist.

Other conservative measures which may not be substituted for those above but which may be used adjunctively can include a home exercise program, activity modification, or facet or epidural injections.
Levels to be treated, e.g. C2-3, C4-6.
Current MRI report/CT Scan report read by an independent radiologist.
A recent neurological exam by the requesting surgeon.
answer.submission_route: Written appeals can be sent by Mail, Fax, or Email to the following state agency: Division of Medicaid Appeals, Idaho Department of Health and Welfare, P.O. Box 83720, Boise, ID 83720-0036; Fax: 1 (208) 364-1811; Email: MedicaidAppeals@dhw.idaho.gov. Appeals or Fair Hearing requests may also be initiated by telephone (1-208-334-0940 or 1-866-681-7062), but written submission is strongly recommended to preserve a paper trail.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Because Idaho Medicaid's quality review organization (Telligen) and Medicaid plans (UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross of Idaho) utilize proprietary, third-party clinical criteria (specifically MCG Health guidelines and McKesson's InterQual criteria), the full, detailed clinical necessity rules are not publicly available to the general public. To obtain the exact medical necessity guidelines applied to this case, the patient or their provider should: (1) Contact Telligen (Idaho Medicaid's QIO) at 1-866-538-9510 or email idmedicaidsupport@telligen.com; (2) Contact Blue Cross of Idaho Customer Service at 1-866-482-2250; or (3) Request the criteria directly from the state's Medical Care Unit at MedicalCareUnit@dhw.idaho.gov.
answer.notes: Although the underlying InterQual and MCG clinical necessity guidelines for Cervical Fusion (CPT 22551) are proprietary and behind login walls, the Blue Cross of Idaho 'Cervical Fusion Prior Authorization Requirements Checklist' is a publicly available document that outlines the clinical documentation required. This checklist serves as an excellent guide for the patient to prepare evidence for their appeal, highlighting the need for detailed physical therapy logs, failed prescription NSAID use, and specific diagnostic imaging reports.

The patient's medical record must contain documentation that fully supports the medical necessity for the requested services. This documentation includes, but is not limited to, relevant medical history, physical examination, and results of pertinent diagnostic tests or procedures. Documentation supporting the medical necessity should be legible, maintained in the patient's medical record, and must be made available upon request. Definitions Dynamic Stabilization: Also called flexible fusion or soft stabilization. A surgical procedure that stabilizes the spine with the insertion of a motion-preserving, flexible implant designed to provide more mobility than traditional spinal fusion. The procedure uses rods, cords, and spacers to stabilize spinal segments and reduce pressure on the intervertebral disc and facet joints (Hayes, 2025). Facet Joint Replacement: Also called total facet arthroplasty. A surgical procedure that replaces the facet joints using flexible materials to stabilize the spine as an alternative to fusion. Isolated Facet Joint Fusion: Also called facet arthrodesis. Facet joint fusion without decompression. A surgical procedure that fuses the facet joint using allograft bone dowels made from donated cortical bone. Staged Multiple Sessions: Includes procedures performed on different days or requiring an additional anesthesia session. result.text: FAQs | Idaho Medicaid Telligen Website Idaho DHW Website Home Document Library Education & Training FAQs Provider News Contact Select Page Frequently Asked Questions Qualitrac LOGIN Provider Portal REGISTER Qualitrac LOGIN Provider Portal REGISTER For FAQs specific to the Children’s Habilitation Intervention Services, click here . For FAQs specific to Post Payment Reviews, click here . FAQs specific to Home Health Reviews, click here. FAQs specific to DMEPOS Reviews, click here. Click on a question below to reveal the answer. What constitutes a “technical denial?” Technical denials are issued when the provider does not submit clinical information or other documentation necessary to complete the review. A technical denial will also be issued when requested information is not submitted within the defined time frame. What medical necessity criteria does Telligen use? All cases must meet Idaho Medicaid criteria before applying any other criteria. Telligen uses MCG criteria. How long does Telligen take to complete reviews? We do our best to review all requests within 72 hours of submission. Telligen’s contract with the Medicaid agency defines the time periods for completing each type of review. Please refer the Provider Manual for the maximum amount of time to complete reviews and remain compliant with contract requirements. What is an urgent review? Telligen works the authorization cases according to the dates they are due as determined by the State of Idaho (see specific turnaround times according to review type on this FAQ page). An authorization request is not considered urgent just because the surgery is scheduled for the next day. URAC (Utilization Review Accreditation Commission shortened to URAC in 1996) defines urgent reviews as any request for a UM recommendation with respect to which the application of the time periods for making non-urgent care recommendations could seriously jeopardize the life or health of the consumer or the ability of the consumer to regain maximum function, OR in the opinion of a physician with knowledge of the consumer’s medical condition, would subject the consumer to severe pain that cannot be adequately managed without the care or treatment that is the subject of the case. If you feel your request falls under the definition of an urgent request, you may call into our Call Center and provide the rationale for this. Please note that Telligen has 3 business days to complete urgent requests. How do providers submit cases for review? Service requests and medical records must be submitted to Telligen in the Qualitrac provider portal. There is no longer an option to fax service requests or records to Telligen. What information is required on MSRP/Invoices for Durable Medical Equipment items? A sufficient MSRP/Invoice must be from the manufacturer of the requested equipment, and it must include the price, a description of the item, and the HCPCS code.
